title: PowerPoint on the web: reference an existing PowerPoint file when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: the briefing says Microsoft has not documented sensitivity-label inheritance, but Purview documents automatic inheritance of the source label and its protection settings for new content created with Copilot in PowerPoint. The roadmap facts and licence-management routes are supported; the broader claim that behaviour beyond the release notes is undocumented also needs narrowing.

claims.claim: This feature lets users reference the content of a PowerPoint file when creating a presentation with Copilot using Agent Mode.
claims.quote: You can now reference the content of a PowerPoint file when creating a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint using Agent Mode.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for this specific Reference file option.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot in PowerPoint Reference file Agent Mode admin disable policy default sign-in consent roles'; '555892 default license admin setting'. Opened release notes, Copilot controls for management, requirements and Edit with Copilot; no option-specific arrival default.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page dedicated to this specific roadmap feature was found beyond its release-note entry.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Agent Mode Reference file existing presentation licensing default sensitivity label inheritance 555892'; 'PowerPoint Agent Mode reference'; '555892 default license admin setting'. Opened release notes; other results describe general Copilot or different agents.

claims.claim: Details of behaviour beyond the release-note entry are not documented.
claims.quote: If you use Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook to create new content based on an item that has a sensitivity label applied, the sensitivity label from the source file is automatically inherited, with the label's protection settings.
claims.fix: Remove 'so details of behaviour beyond that entry are not documented'. General Microsoft Purview guidance documents behaviour that covers this case, including sensitivity-label inheritance, at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-m365-copilot.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions: sensitivity label
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes no sensitivity-label carry-over for new decks created from referenced content.
claims.quote: If you use Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook to create new content based on an item that has a sensitivity label applied, the sensitivity label from the source file is automatically inherited, with the label's protection settings.
claims.fix: Replace the label absence with: 'Microsoft Purview documents that new content created with Copilot in PowerPoint from a labelled source automatically inherits the source sensitivity label and its protection settings.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-m365-copilot. Remove the open question asking how the source sensitivity label affects the new deck; retain the advice to check its label before sharing.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented source sharing-permission carry-over specifically for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot PowerPoint reference existing presentation sensitivity label inherit new presentation'; 'PowerPoint reference label Copilot inheritance'. Opened release notes and Purview ai-m365-copilot: label protection inheritance is stated, but copying source sharing grants is not.
